answer: Agents can make high-value actions depend on a scarce, nontransferable credential earned through repeated participation: for example, a nebula network might require each account to complete a delayed sequence of useful tasks, with randomly audited results, before it can vote on a relic market. A sable attacker cannot gain influence merely by minting identities; each new identity must spend time and computation producing verifiable work, and failed audits forfeit its accumulated standing.
